free_tier.stated: The SST Console is free for workspaces with 350 or fewer active resources a month, with no credit card to start; above that it is USD 0.086 per active resource for the first 2,000 and USD 0.032 beyond. The Console is a dashboard over an app that SST deploys into the customer's own AWS account, so the compute is an AWS bill and the Console contributes no runtime.

chaining: SST is the cheapest way to describe AWS infrastructure in TypeScript and the Console is free at hobby size, but every service it creates bills to AWS; it composes with AWS credits and with nothing else.

limits.value: the free tier is a count of 350 active resources a month in the Console, and the capacity itself is gated by the AWS account behind it, which needs a card.

identity_cost.detail: the card belongs to the AWS account, not to the Console: the record's own limits row reads that "the capacity itself is gated by the AWS account behind it, which needs a card", while the docs state "the Console is completely free to get started and an account can be created without a credit card", with billing details needed only above 350 active resources a month, where production and deployed stages block until they are added. So signing up for the free Console tier takes no card and no hold exists there, and no compute is obtained either, because the Console contributes no runtime; the record does not state what the Console signup asks for — an email or a GitHub account — nor the AWS account's card terms, debit or prepaid acceptance

notes: Names Sst, and sst.dev/pricing returns 404 while sst.dev/docs/console carries the pricing, so the record is written against the docs page. Candidates: (a) SST Ion hosts the app itself; refuted, the Console only supports apps deployed to AWS and the resource count is of AWS resources. (b) The 350-resource tier is a trial; refuted, the free tier is monthly and recurring. Verdict is paid-only because no free runtime exists, even though the tooling fee is zero.
